mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.00% in the month preceding the forecast period coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.00% in the preceding month
regime_hint: Rising inflationary bias in the Fed’s policy framework
failure_condition: Over a 36-month window, no significant negative 20-day forward returns accompany FEDFUNDS > 5.00% in the prior month (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in PAYEMS (labor market additions) of at least 20,000 jobs for three consecutive months predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as expanding labor demand supports corporate earnings growth.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥20,000 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: Across 10 such labor expansion windows, the 60-day forward return mean is not statistically higher than the pre-expansion period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both HOUST (residential construction) and INDPRO (industrial production) by at least 10% in the prior month signals a demand-dampening structural shock, producing a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: Both HOUST and INDPRO fall by ≥10% in the previous month
failure_condition: In 5 such dual-index declines, the 20-day forward return mean is not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in INDPRO (industrial production) of at least 15% followed by a subsequent rise of at least 8% within the next two months predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as the market anticipates supply-side recovery.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by ≥15% in month t, then rises by ≥8% in month t+1
failure_condition: Over 4 such recovery patterns, the 20-day forward return mean is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in UNRATE (unemployment rate) below 4.5% for two consecutive months, amid rising CPIAUCSL (CPI), signals a disinflationary shift that supports risk-on sentiment and a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.5% for two consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL rising
failure_condition: In 10 such UNRATE-CPIAUCSL patterns, the 5-day forward return mean is not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payrolls surprise exceeding +100,000 jobs for three consecutive months in a non-recession regime is associated with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals robust labor absorption.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS surprise > +100,000 for three consecutive months AND regime: no recession
failure_condition: Across 8 such positive surprise windows, the 60-day forward return mean is not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both GDPC1 (GDP) and RSAFS (retail sales) by at least 2% in the prior quarter, without a compensating rise in HOUST, predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as demand softens.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 ↓ ≥2%, RSAFS ↓ ≥2%, HOUST does not rise ≥3% in the same quarter
failure_condition: In 6 such demand contractions, the 20-day forward return mean is not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in FEDFUNDS below 4.00% for four consecutive months in a non-inflationary regime is associated with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as lower policy rates reduce borrowing costs.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 4.00% for four consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL < 105
failure_condition: Over 7 such low-rate periods, the 60-day forward return mean is not significantly higher than the pre-accommodative period (t-test p > 0.05).
